subject: Evaluation signal lifecycle + cutover checklist for FastPass MAP
messages:
From: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@fastpass.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Connors <sara.connors@fastpass.ai>
Date: 2025-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: FastPass MAP & evaluation window

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency profile and the cost breakdown. We need a consolidated Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation window, explicit success criteria, and the acceptance tests we'll run. Procurement also wants clear exit gates and rollback thresholds up front so they can sign off.

Can your team draft a MAP + acceptance checklist we can use for our internal signoffs? Ideal evaluation window is mid-August (two weeks) and we'd like to avoid surprises at cutover.

Two specific asks from our side:
- A small list of deterministic acceptance tests (smoke + regression) we can run against our sample dataset.
- Clear P95 latency and cost per 1k tokens targets (or a decision ladder if we need fallback models).

Thanks — if you can send a first draft today or tomorrow that'd be great.

— Alejandro
CIO, FastPass AI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@fastpass.ai>
Cc: Sara Connors <sara.connors@fastpass.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: FastPass MAP & evaluation window

Alejandro — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP summary and an outline of acceptance tests (see acceptance-test-cases.md). High-level items below; I put the proposed evaluation window at Aug 4–18 to give both teams time for staging validation.

Proposed Success Criteria (high level):
- Functional correctness: >98% pass rate on the regression prompt set (we'll provide the runner).
- Latency: P95 <= 220ms for 512-token average prompt (staging).
- Cost: token cost (inference only) <= $0.20 per 1k tokens with configured batching and KV cache.
- Reliability: <1% error rate (5xx or model timeouts) across the two-week window.
- Security/compliance: audit logs present for every request; no egress to external third-party endpoints.

Exit gates (go / no-go):
- Go: All above criteria met in staging run for 48h continuous traffic simulation, and smoke checks in production shadow for 24h.
- No-go / Rollback trigger: any single-day P95 spike > 2x target OR >5% error rate in production shadow.

Acceptance test categories (attached more granular):
1) Smoke: basic generation, auth, error handling (5 tests)
2) Performance: P95 latency, throughput saturations, KV warm-up behavior (6 tests)
3) Cost simulation: closed-loop token accounting under 1k-100k token mixes
4) Security: audit log ingestion, key rotation validation

Attachments: FastPass_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP timeline + owners), acceptance-test-cases.md (test definitions), network-diagram.png (recommended VPC peering).

Next steps: Marcus/Ben — can you confirm the feasibility of the P95 target on our Dedicated infra and the KV cache warm-up test? Alejandro/Sara — if those look ok we'll finalize the MAP and provide DocuSign + HubSpot links for approvals.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: FastPass MAP & evaluation window

Kimberly — quick tech notes from runtime side (cc Laura for staging ops):

I like the targets but propose these clarifications to make acceptance deterministic: 
- Specify sequence-length distribution for the P95 test (we should run at 64/256/512 splits).
- Add an explicit KV cache-warmup acceptance: P95 should drop by at least 30% after 3 warmup calls per UUID. This avoids surprises at the start of a ramp.
- Cost target needs a reference quant (e.g., int8 quantized model + batching 8) — otherwise it’s not actionable. Suggest we call out baseline config: quantized v1, batch=8, dynamic batching enabled.
- Audit logs: provide a sha256 hash sample of first 100 lines for us to validate ingestion (procurement likes deterministic proof).

Operational checklist addition:
- Staging shadow run must include a synthetic traffic generator that replays 6-hour peak slices from your provided corpus.
- We should reserve two Dedicated nodes for the first 48h of the eval window to prevent noisy neighbor issues.

Ben/Laura — can you add these to the accept-test doc and confirm node reservation timeline?

— Marcus
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-21T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: FastPass MAP & evaluation window

Adding operational checklist + schedule. I'm drafting acceptance-test-cases.md updates now (will attach final version in the MAP). Key items I added: 

Cutover smoke plan (three phases):
- Dev: run smoke suite against sample dataset (sanity) — pass required before staging.
- Staging: 48h continuous run with synthetic peak slices; validate P95 across defined sequence-length buckets; verify KV warm-up strategy.
- Prod shadow: 24h production traffic shadow (no traffic routing) with alerting on thresholds.

Decision matrix (color-coded):
- Green: all pass -> schedule cutover date (T+2 business days).
- Yellow: one non-critical fail (functional regression <2%) -> mitigation plan + extended 48h run.
- Red: any critical fail (P95 >2x OR >5% error rate) -> rollback and root-cause engagement.

I've also included exact curl commands for smoke tests and a small runner script for KV cache warmup.

Laura — can you confirm we can reserve 2 Dedicated nodes Aug 3–6 and again Aug 10–12 for stress runs? If yes, I'll bake that into the MAP timeline.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@fastpass.ai>, Sara Connors <sara.connors@fastpass.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-22T14:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: FastPass MAP & evaluation window

Alejandro / Sara — consolidated MAP attached (FastPass_MAP_v3.xlsx) and the updated acceptance-test-cases.md. Highlights:

- Evaluation window: Aug 4 00:00 UTC — Aug 18 23:59 UTC.
- Owners: Kimberly (Redwood MAP owner), Ben (runtime tests + smoke), Marcus (performance QC), Sara (FastPass test data & procurement owner).
- Exact test definitions: see acceptance-test-cases.md (includes sequence-length buckets: 64/256/512).
- Node reservations: Laura confirmed (2 Dedicated nodes Aug 3–6, and Aug 10–12) — staging ops ready.
- Artifacts for procurement: sample audit log SHA + SOC2 extract attached.

DocuSign link for MAP signature: https://docusign.example/FP-MAP-v3
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/record/FP-2025-0427

Please review the MAP and the attached test cases. Two ask items from my side before we finalize:
1) FastPass to confirm the representative prompt set and provide the synthetic peak slices for the staging generator (file list ok via secure upload).
2) Procurement to confirm the acceptable rollback SLA (we propose the rollback trigger from the decision matrix).

If OK, we'll send the DocuSign package and lock the evaluation nodes.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: FastPass_MAP_v3.xlsx; acceptance-test-cases.md; network-diagram.png)
From: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@fastpass.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sara Connors <sara.connors@fastpass.ai>, procurement@fastpass.ai
Date: 2025-07-23T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: FastPass MAP & evaluation window

Kimberly / team — this looks good, appreciate the thoroughness. A few quick notes from procurement & ops: 

- FastPass accepts the evaluation window Aug 4–18. We'll upload the representative prompt set and the 6-hour peak slices to the secure bucket by EOD Friday (link will be shared).
- Procurement: please note one small change to the rollback SLA — can we change the single-day P95 spike trigger from >2x to >1.8x? If Redwood can accept that tighter rollback threshold we can sign the MAP this week.
- Attached is our SOC2 extract (FastPass_SOC2_Q1.pdf) and procurement has started their internal review; procurement@fastpass.ai is the contact for any follow-up.

If Redwood confirms the rollback threshold update I'll route DocuSign and we can lock the node reservations.

— Alejandro
CIO, FastPass AI
